global.headline: US AND IRAN PAUSE STRIKES FOR SECOND STRAIGHT NIGHT AS HORMUZ TALKS ADVANCE; PENTAGON RESTORES DEATH TOLL TO 18, WOUNDED JUMPS TO 624
summary: Neither the US nor Iran carried out strikes for a second consecutive night, after CENTCOM abruptly suspended its 13-night bombing campaign late Friday. US envoy Mike Waltz said negotiators were engaged "at every level," though Trump maintained the military remained "locked and loaded." The pause followed a recommendation from the top US military commander in the Middle East that continued strikes around the Strait of Hormuz had reached the limit of their effectiveness. A senior Iranian official told Reuters Tehran would hold its own fire as long as the US pause holds. Deputy foreign ministers from Iran and Oman held two days of talks in Tehran on mechanisms for safe commercial passage through Hormuz while respecting Iran's claimed coastal-water rights; two regional sources said the talks were constructive and heading in a positive direction, though not yet concluded. Brent crude fell 7.6% to $90.95/barrel on the de-escalation signal, though still up roughly 10% for the week.

Separately, the Pentagon updated its official war-casualty database Saturday, restoring the four service members killed in Jordan and Iraq that had briefly vanished from the count earlier in the week. The confirmed US death toll is now 18, and the wounded count jumped to 624 — over 140 more than the 482 figure tracked as recently as last week — under a newly added "Overseas Operations" category backdated to 7 July. The scale of the revision reignited the funding fight in Congress: House Speaker Mike Johnson called Democratic resistance to further Pentagon funding "shameful" amid concerns US munitions stockpiles are being depleted, as the chamber's own $95bn war-budget resolution remains stalled in the Senate.
global.geopolitical: A second strike-free night alongside genuine progress in Oman-mediated Hormuz talks is the clearest de-escalation signal since the ceasefire's collapse in early July, but Iran's halt is explicitly conditional and Trump's "locked and loaded" framing keeps resumption on the table; the sharply revised casualty count, meanwhile, undercuts Washington's ability to claim a clean, low-cost war just as it seeks more money to sustain it.
global.socioeconomic: Brent's 7.6% one-day drop shows how quickly trade-dependent economies like Singapore's could see relief if the pause holds, but the whiplash of the past month — over $100 one week, under $91 the next — makes near-term energy-cost planning difficult for importers and airlines alike.

global.headline: BERLIN PRIDE ATTACK SUSPECT KILLED BY POLICE AFTER 20-HOUR MANHUNT; PRIOR CONVICTION FOR ATTEMPTING TO JOIN ISIS EMERGES
summary: German police shot dead 21-year-old Abdul Ballout, the suspect in Saturday's van-ramming attack on Berlin's Pride parade, after he charged at officers with a bladed weapon in a garden in the western district of Spandau around 6pm Sunday, roughly 20 hours after the attack. Ballout, born in Germany to a family of Lebanese origin, had a prior conviction: he received a suspended sentence of one year and ten months in youth custody in May for attempting to travel to Syria to join Islamic State, preparing a serious act of violence, and disseminating IS propaganda. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said "everything we see here points to us dealing with an Islamic terror attack." The confirmed toll from Saturday's attack stands at one dead and 29 injured; the parade was cancelled mid-event.
global.geopolitical: A confirmed prior Islamist-extremism conviction, on a suspended youth sentence, will sharpen scrutiny of Germany's handling of known radicalisation cases and add to a broader European debate over vehicle-ramming attacks at public gatherings.
global.socioeconomic: Beyond the immediate toll, the cancellation of one of Europe's largest Pride events is likely to reignite pressure on German and European cities to invest in vehicle-barrier security at major public gatherings.

global.headline: EUROPEAN WILDFIRES THREATEN BORDEAUX AS 300,000+ FLEE HOMES ACROSS FRANCE AND SPAIN
summary: Wildfires fanned by extreme heat and strong winds advanced to within roughly 15km of Bordeaux, France's wine-region capital, Bordeaux Mayor Thomas Cazenave said, as the death toll and evacuation figures from Spain and France's worst wildfire season in years continued climbing. More than 300,000 people have now fled their homes across both countries — about 220,000 in France and over 75,000 in Spain, with a further 30,000 Spaniards ordered to shelter in place. France deployed a giant A400M military transport aircraft to drop flame retardant over the drought-hit Gironde region, alongside 1,400 firefighters. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez warned "difficult hours lie ahead" as hotter weather looms; vineyards in the Bordeaux area have not yet been damaged, with this year's grapes still too small to absorb smoke taint.
global.geopolitical: A wildfire season severe enough to threaten a major European city and displace 300,000+ people across two EU states is likely to intensify pressure within the bloc for coordinated climate-adaptation and firefighting-resource-sharing arrangements.
global.socioeconomic: Beyond the immediate humanitarian toll, a fire approaching Bordeaux itself threatens the tourism and hospitality economy of one of the world's most famous wine regions at the height of summer, even as the crop itself remains unaffected so far.

global.headline: ISRAELI SETTLERS TORCH WEST BANK MOSQUES IN REVENGE ATTACKS AFTER DEADLY NABLUS-AREA CLASH
summary: Israeli settlers set fire to at least two mosques and vandalised cars and farmland in villages near Nablus early Sunday, a day after Israeli forces launched a clampdown — arresting around 50 Palestinians and raiding roughly 70 homes — in response to Friday's shootout in the village of Tal that killed four Palestinians and two Israelis, one of them a local security coordinator. In the village of Qusra, southeast of Nablus, settlers torched a newly completed mosque and sprayed Hebrew graffiti reading "Jewish revenge" along with the name of one of the Israelis killed at Tal, village council head Abdel Azim Wadi said. No action has been announced against the settlers involved in either the original Tal incursion or Sunday's arson. The UN and Palestinian Authority say dozens of Palestinians have been killed and hundreds wounded in escalating settler violence this year.
global.geopolitical: Settler arson explicitly invoking "revenge," following a clampdown that targeted Palestinians rather than the settlers whose incursion triggered Friday's deadly clash, deepens Palestinian accusations of official impunity for settler violence and further strains an already volatile West Bank security situation.
global.socioeconomic: Destroyed religious and agricultural property compounds economic hardship for West Bank communities already squeezed by recurring closures, movement restrictions and settlement expansion.

global.headline: ISRAEL APPROVES INTERNATIONAL FORCE FOR GAZA AS NETANYAHU HEADS TO WASHINGTON
summary: Israel's security cabinet approved a legal framework allowing an International Stabilization Force — initially around 200 troops from countries including Uganda, Morocco and Indonesia — to enter parts of Gaza outside Israeli control, an Israeli official said Sunday, a concrete step under Trump's ceasefire plan after months of stalled Gaza governance arrangements. The force is intended to secure Gaza's borders and train local police as Israeli troops gradually withdraw from areas it patrols; Israel retains the right to approve which countries may contribute troops. Netanyahu is due to fly to Washington on Monday to meet Trump on Tuesday. Separately Sunday, Netanyahu accused New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani of "fomenting hate" after Mamdani said in a video message that Netanyahu, wanted on an ICC warrant, was "not welcome" in New York; Netanyahu called the ICC charges "bogus" and said he still intends to address the UN General Assembly in the city in September.
global.geopolitical: A concrete, if still narrow, first deployment framework moves the long-stalled Gaza governance handoff forward for the first time in months, though Israel's retained veto over troop-contributing countries and the still-undefined boundary of "areas beyond Israeli control" leave plenty of room for the process to stall again.
global.socioeconomic: Any real move toward a functioning Gaza security and policing structure is a precondition for reconstruction and aid delivery to resume at scale, after nearly two years of governance paralysis have left the territory's economy in ruins.

singapore.headline: SINGAPORE CONDEMNS HOUTHI ATTACKS ON SAUDI ARABIA, URGES ALL PARTIES TO EXERCISE RESTRAINT
summary: Singapore's Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the Iran-aligned Houthis' weekend missile and drone attacks on Saudi Aramco's Jizan and Yanbu oil facilities on the Red Sea coast, urging all parties in the region to exercise restraint to prevent further escalation. The statement follows a pattern of Singapore MFA interventions this month as the Iran war's fronts have widened to threaten Gulf and Red Sea energy infrastructure directly.
singapore.geopolitical: As a small, trade-dependent state with no direct stake in the conflict, Singapore's public calls for restraint are a low-cost but consistent diplomatic signal, reflecting how directly an escalating Middle East energy-infrastructure war now touches states far from the region.
singapore.socioeconomic: Continued attacks on Saudi refining and export capacity, on top of the Hormuz disruption, keep global oil-price volatility elevated — a direct cost concern for an import-dependent economy still absorbing record COE and electricity-tariff prints.

singapore.headline: PAP WOMEN'S WING PROPOSES ENHANCED CHILDCARE LEAVE AFTER PUBLIC ENGAGEMENTS
summary: The PAP Women's Wing, led by Gan Siow Huang, put forward enhanced childcare leave among a set of proposals arising from a round of public engagements, flagging that parents with more children, or older children, tend not to have enough childcare leave under current entitlements. The proposals add to a running theme this month of family-support policy activity, following the Youth Plan launch and the Community Care Apartments changes.
singapore.socioeconomic: A push for more generous childcare leave lands directly on the same cost-of-living and family-formation anxieties this pipeline has tracked all month via the record-low 0.87 total fertility rate and rising retrenchment/wrongful-dismissal claims, adding pressure for the government's next Budget cycle to address caregiving support more structurally rather than incrementally.

singapore.headline: TAN BOON LIAT BUILDING SOLD FOR S$950M IN SINGAPORE'S BIGGEST EN BLOC DEAL OF 2026
summary: The 15-storey freehold Tan Boon Liat Building at 315 Outram Road, above Havelock MRT station, has been sold en bloc to Kingsford Havelock Pte Ltd, a unit of Kingsford Group, for S$950 million — Singapore's largest collective-sale transaction so far this year, surpassing the S$880 million Loyang Valley deal in April. The site was first put up for sale about a year ago at an asking price of S$1.15 billion without success, then relaunched in February at a reduced reserve of S$1 billion after crossing the 80% owner-consensus threshold; the final price still came in below that reserve. The sale still requires owners' approval at an upcoming extraordinary general meeting and Strata Titles Board approval.
singapore.socioeconomic: A near-billion-dollar collective sale closing well below its original asking price, after a failed first attempt, signals continued but more price-realistic momentum in Singapore's en bloc market as sellers adjust expectations to current borrowing costs and buyer appetite.

word.definition: To kill or destroy, especially by fire, often as or evoking a sacrifice; to offer up as a sacrificial victim.
word.etymology: From Latin immolare ("to sprinkle with sacrificial meal, to sacrifice"), from in- ("upon") + mola ("sacrificial meal, ground grain"), referring to the grain scattered over a victim before slaughter in Roman ritual.
word.example: In Qusra, settlers immolated a newly completed mosque and daubed its scorched walls with the words "Jewish revenge" — turning an act of arson into a ritual gesture, a sacrifice offered to grief rather than to any god.
